neighbours.label: Credential adjective naming a qualified professional (licensed, certified, registered) in staffing or service text, vs plain or descriptive adjectives in the same slot
fire: All of our massage therapists are licensed and insured in Oregon.
The hospital is hiring two registered nurses for the night shift.
Ask a certified financial planner before you move your savings.
Each crew is led by a licensed plumber with ten years of work.
The school employs a registered psychologist for its students.
Only a certified welder may repair the pressure tank.
We send a licensed inspector to check the roof before sale.
The ward is staffed by registered midwives around the clock.
quiet: All of our massage therapists are friendly and patient in Oregon.
The hospital is hiring two young nurses for the night shift.
Ask a trusted old friend before you move your savings.
Each crew is led by a cheerful plumber with ten years of work.
The school employs a new psychologist for its students.
Only a careful welder may repair the pressure tank.
We send a quick inspector to check the roof before sale.
The ward is staffed by kind midwives around the clock.

predictions: Credential adjectives 0.2-0.45; plain adjectives in the same slot under 0.15. Staffing context alone gave 0.15, so the margin is narrow.
notes: Card: ' private' in 'our private duty nurses' (165), ' Certified', ' certified', ' licensed'.
